title: Probe-based reranking A/B control and per-customer NDCG/MRR instrumentation
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Goal: add a lightweight probe-based A/B control surface to the reranking endpoint and instrument per-customer NDCG/MRR so we can measure small quality deltas in real traffic without increasing latency or storage costs significantly. Background: Customers run reranked results on embeddings with downstream scoring and we currently lack stable per-customer ranking metrics (NDCG/MRR) and A/B hooks that operate at production sampling rates. This ticket implements an exposure probe, offline/online eval pipeline integration, and telemetry schema for quality+latency trade-offs.
approach: 1) Add a sampling probe that records candidate lists, final ranks, and gold labels (when available) to a compact protobuf event emitted asynchronously. 2) Integrate the probe with our existing eval harness to compute daily NDCG@k and MRR slices per-customer and per-promptset. 3) Provide A/B exposure hooks so routing policies can mark requests as control/variant and include the probe payload. 4) Keep probe path nonblocking and size-limited (max 8 candidates, 2KB payload cap) to protect latency SLOs. 5) Add dashboards and alerting for significant regressions and divergence across segments.
acceptance_criteria: Probe emitted for >=1% sample of rerank traffic with payload size <2KB on median
Daily NDCG@10 and MRR computed and stored per-customer for sampled traffic
A/B exposure flag present end-to-end and available in evaluation pipeline
No >5% increase in p50 p99 latency for rerank endpoint in canary traffic
Dashboard panels for top 10 customers and overall delta, with alert on >0.02 NDCG drop
implementation_notes: - Use compact event schema: request_id, customer_id (hashed), probe_version, candidates[score, id], chosen_index, label_hint(optional), routing_tag. - Emit events to kinesis-redwood-rank-probes; downstream job will compress and write to s3 for batch eval. - Keep PII out of probe payload; hash customer_id and strip user-level text. - Use existing A/B framework: attach exposure=rerank_probe_v1 tag to requests.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Sampling bias: small sample may miss long-tail customers. Storage costs vs fidelity: we trim candidate features to reduce size which might reduce offline diagnostic power. Privacy: we intentionally avoid storing raw prompts; that limits some evals. Rolling out for a small percent reduces risk but increases time to detect regressions.
performance_tests: Canary run on staging for 12h with 5% sample: median added CPU <1%, p50 latency +1.8%, p99 +3.4% under typical load. End-to-end eval job completed processing 10M probe events in 2.1h on batch cluster. Results stored in s3://redwood-evals/2025-02-24/probes/.
next_steps: 1) Land PR for probe emitter (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/pull/1427). 2) Wire kinesis stream and batch consumer (ENG-91235). 3) Add dashboard panels and alerts (ENG-91236). 4) Schedule 1% production canary for two weeks then ramp based on metrics.
